content.text:
1	---
     2	name: file-reading
     3	description: "Use this skill when a file has been uploaded but its content is NOT in your context — only its path at /mnt/user-data/uploads/ is listed in an uploaded_files block. This skill is a router: it tells you which tool to use for each file type (pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, json, images, archives, ebooks) so you read the right amount the right way instead of blindly running cat on a binary. Triggers: any mention of /mnt/user-data/uploads/, an uploaded_files section, a file_path tag, or a user asking about an uploaded file you have not yet read. Do NOT use this skill if the file content is already visible in your context inside a documents block — you already have it."
     4	compatibility: "claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cowork — any surface where uploads land at /mnt/user-data/uploads/"
     5	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Reading Uploaded Files
     9	
    10	## Why this skill exists
    11	
    12	When a user uploads a file in claude.ai, Claude Desktop, or Cowork,
    13	the file is written to `/mnt/user-data/uploads/<filename>` and you are told the path
    14	in an `<uploaded_files>` block. **The content is not in your context.**
    15	You must go read it.
    16	
    17	The naive thing — `cat /mnt/user-data/uploads/whatever` — is wrong for
    18	most files:
    19	
    20	- On a PDF it prints binary garbage.
    21	- On a 100MB CSV it floods your context with rows you will never use.
    22	- On a DOCX it prints the raw ZIP bytes.
    23	- On an image it does nothing useful at all.
    24	
    25	This skill tells you the right first move for each type, and when to
    26	hand off to a deeper skill.
    27	
    28	## General protocol
    29	
    30	1. **Look at the extension.** That is your dispatch key.
    31	2. **Stat before you read.** Large files need sampling, not slurping.
    32	   ```bash
    33	   stat -c '%s bytes, %y' /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    34	   file /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    35	   ```
    36	3. **Read just enough to answer the user's question.** If they asked
    37	   "how many rows are in this CSV", don't load the whole thing into
    38	   pandas — `wc -l` gives a fast approximation (it counts newlines,
    39	   not CSV records, so it may over-count if quoted fields contain
    40	   embedded newlines).
    41	4. **If a dedicated skill exists, go read it.** The table below tells
    42	   you when. The dedicated skills cover editing, creating, and advanced
    43	   operations that this skill does not.
    44	
    45	## `extract-text`
    46	
    47	For docx, odt, epub, xlsx, pptx, rtf, and ipynb the first move is
    48	`extract-text <file>`. It emits markdown for docx/odt/epub (headings,
    49	bold, lists, links, tables), tab-separated rows under `## Sheet:`
    50	headers for xlsx, text under `## Slide N` headers for pptx, fenced
    51	code cells for ipynb, and plain text for rtf. Pass `--format <fmt>`
    52	when the extension is wrong or absent (e.g., `--format xlsx` on an
    53	`.xlsm`). If it errors on a file, `pandoc <file> -t plain` is a
    54	fallback; for xlsx/pptx, fall back to the dedicated skill's
    55	Python-based approach (openpyxl / python-pptx).
    56	
    57	## Dispatch table
    58	
    59	Where a dedicated skill is named below, invoke it by name if you have a
    60	Skill tool, or Read its SKILL.md (listed in your available skills, or in
    61	the same skills directory as this file).
    62	
    63	| Extension                         | First move                                           | Dedicated skill |
    64	| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
    65	| `.pdf`                            | Content inventory (see PDF section)                  | `pdf-reading`   |
    66	| `.docx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `docx`          |
    67	| `.doc` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.docx` first                             | `docx`          |
    68	| `.xlsx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `xlsx`          |
    69	| `.xlsm`                           | `extract-text --format xlsx`                         | `xlsx`          |
    70	| `.xls` (legacy)                   | `pd.read_excel(engine="xlrd")` — openpyxl rejects it | `xlsx`          |
    71	| `.ods`                            | `pd.read_excel(engine="odf")` — openpyxl rejects it  | `xlsx`          |
    72	| `.pptx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `pptx`          |
    73	| `.ppt` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.pptx` first                             | `pptx`          |
    74	| `.csv`, `.tsv`                    | `pandas` with `nrows`                                | — (below)       |
    75	| `.json`, `.jsonl`                 | `jq` for structure                                   | — (below)       |
    76	| `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp`   | Already in your context as vision input              | — (below)       |
    77	| `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`         | List contents, do **not** auto-extract               | — (below)       |
    78	| `.gz` (single file)               | `zcat \| head` — no manifest to list                 | — (below)       |
    79	| `.epub`, `.odt`                   | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    80	| `.rtf`                            | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    81	| `.ipynb`                          | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    82	| `.txt`, `.md`, `.log`, code files | `wc -c` then `head` or full `cat`                    | — (below)       |
    83	| Unknown                           | `file` then decide                                   | —               |
    84	
    85	---
    86	
    87	## PDF
    88	
    89	**Never** `cat` a PDF — it prints binary garbage.
    90	
    91	Quick first move — get the page count and determine whether the PDF
    92	has an extractable text layer:
    93	
    94	```bash
    95	pdfinfo /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    96	pdffonts /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    97	```
    98	
    99	`pdffonts` tells you whether text extraction will work before you try it:
   100	
   101	- **No fonts listed** (empty table, just the header) → the PDF is a
   102	  scan or raster export. `pdftotext` and `PdfReader.extract_text()`
   103	  will return nothing useful. Go straight to page rasterization or OCR
   104	  — see the `pdf-reading` skill → "Scanned documents".
   105	- **Fonts listed** → there is a text layer; extract it:
   106	  ```bash
   107	  pdftotext -f 1 -l 1 /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf - | head -20
   108	  ```
   109	
   110	The reason to check `pdffonts` first is user-facing: running
   111	`pdftotext` on a scan produces an empty result, and in a visible
   112	transcript that reads as a failed first attempt before you fall back
   113	to OCR. The two-line diagnostic above costs one tool call and avoids
   114	that — you arrive at the right method on the first try, which is what
   115	a user perceives as "it just read my file."
   116	
   117	That also shapes how to open your reply. The diagnostic commands are
   118	plumbing, not content; lead with what the user asked about. On a
   119	scanned receipt that might be "This is a 3-page scanned invoice; the
   120	amount due on page 2 is $1,845.00," and on a digitally-authored report
   121	it might be "The Q3 report runs 28 pages; revenue on p. 4 is $12.3M,
   122	up 9% YoY." What you're steering away from is the "I'll examine the
   123	PDF" / "Let me check if this is extractable" preamble — the answer to
   124	their question is the first thing they should see.
   125	
   126	For anything beyond a quick peek — figures, tables, attachments,
   127	forms, scanned PDFs, visual inspection, or choosing a reading strategy
   128	— go read the `pdf-reading` skill. It covers content inventory, text
   129	extraction vs. page rasterization, embedded content extraction, and
   130	document-type-aware reading strategies.
   131	
   132	For PDF form filling, creation, merging, splitting, or watermarking,
   133	go read the `pdf` skill.
   134	
   135	---
   136	
   137	## DOCX / DOC
   138	
   139	The `docx` skill covers editing, creating, tracked changes, images.
   140	Read it if you need any of those. For a quick look:
   141	
   142	```bash
   143	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/memo.docx | head -200
   144	```
   145	
   146	Legacy `.doc` (not `.docx`) must be converted first — see the `docx`
   147	skill.
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## XLSX / XLS / spreadsheets
   152	
   153	The `xlsx` skill covers formulas, formatting, charts, creating. Read
   154	it if you need any of those. For a quick look at an `.xlsx`:
   155	
   156	```bash
   157	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx | head -100
   158	```
   159	
   160	For `.xlsm`, add `--format xlsx` (same zip structure; only the
   161	extension differs). When you need a structured preview in Python:
   162	
   163	```python
   164	from openpyxl import load_workbook
   165	wb = load_workbook("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx", read_only=True)
   166	print("Sheets:", wb.sheetnames)
   167	ws = wb.active
   168	for row in ws.iter_rows(max_row=5, values_only=True):
   169	    print(row)
   170	```
   171	
   172	`read_only=True` matters — without it, openpyxl loads the entire
   173	workbook into memory, which breaks on large files. Do not trust
   174	`ws.max_row` in read-only mode: many non-Excel writers omit the
   175	dimension record, so it comes back `None` or wrong. If you need a row
   176	count, iterate or use pandas.
   177	
   178	**Legacy `.xls`** — openpyxl raises `InvalidFileException`. Use:
   179	
   180	```python
   181	import pandas as pd
   182	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/old.xls", engine="xlrd", nrows=5)
   183	```
   184	
   185	**`.ods` (OpenDocument)** — openpyxl also rejects this. Use:
   186	
   187	```python
   188	import pandas as pd
   189	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.ods", engine="odf", nrows=5)
   190	```
   191	
   192	---
   193	
   194	## PPTX
   195	
   196	```bash
   197	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/deck.pptx | head -200
   198	```
   199	
   200	**Legacy `.ppt`** — convert to `.pptx` first via LibreOffice; see the
   201	`pptx` skill for the sandbox-safe `scripts/office/soffice.py` wrapper
   202	(bare `soffice` hangs here because the seccomp filter blocks the
   203	`AF_UNIX` sockets LibreOffice uses for instance management).
   204	
   205	For anything beyond reading, go to the `pptx` skill.
   206	
   207	---
   208	
   209	## CSV / TSV
   210	
   211	**Do not** `cat` or `head` these blindly. A CSV with a 50KB quoted cell
   212	in row 1 will wreck your `head -5`. Use pandas with `nrows`:
   213	
   214	```python
   215	import pandas as pd
   216	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv", nrows=5)
   217	print(df)
   218	print()
   219	print(df.dtypes)
   220	```
   221	
   222	Approximate row count without loading (over-counts if the file has
   223	RFC-4180 quoted newlines — the same quoted-cell case this section
   224	warned about above):
   225	
   226	```bash
   227	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv
   228	```
   229	
   230	Full analysis only after you know the shape:
   231	
   232	```python
   233	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv")
   234	print(df.describe())
   235	```
   236	
   237	TSV: same, with `sep="\t"`.
   238	
   239	---
   240	
   241	## JSON / JSONL
   242	
   243	Structure first, content second:
   244	
   245	```bash
   246	jq 'type' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   247	jq 'if type == "array" then length elif type == "object" then keys else . end' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   248	```
   249	
   250	(`keys` errors on scalar JSON roots — a bare `"hello"` or `42` is valid
   251	JSON per RFC 7159 — so guard the branch.)
   252	
   253	Then drill into what the user actually asked about.
   254	
   255	JSONL (one object per line) — do **not** `jq` the whole file; work line
   256	by line:
   257	
   258	```bash
   259	head -3 /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl | jq .
   260	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl
   261	```
   262	
   263	---
   264	
   265	## Images (JPG / PNG / GIF / WEBP)
   266	
   267	**You can already see uploaded images.** They are injected into your
   268	context as vision inputs alongside the `<uploaded_files>` pointer. You
   269	do not need to read them from disk to describe them.
   270	
   271	The disk copy is only needed if you are going to **process** the image
   272	programmatically:
   273	
   274	```python
   275	from PIL import Image
   276	img = Image.open("/mnt/user-data/uploads/photo.jpg")
   277	print(img.size, img.mode, img.format)
   278	```
   279	
   280	For OCR on an image (text extraction, not description):
   281	
   282	```python
   283	import pytesseract
   284	print(pytesseract.image_to_string(img))
   285	```
   286	
   287	Note: the client resizes images larger than 2000×2000 down to that
   288	bound and re-encodes as JPEG before upload, so the disk copy may not
   289	be the user's original bytes. For most processing this doesn't matter;
   290	if the user is asking about original-resolution pixel data, flag it.
   291	
   292	---
   293	
   294	## Archives (ZIP / TAR / TAR.GZ)
   295	
   296	**List first. Extract never — unless the user explicitly asks.**
   297	Archives can be huge, contain path traversal, or nest forever.
   298	
   299	```bash
   300	unzip -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.zip
   301	tar -tf /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.tar
   302	```
   303	
   304	GNU tar auto-detects compression — `tar -tf` works on `.tar`,
   305	`.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz` alike. Don't hard-code `-z`.
   306	
   307	If the user wants one file from inside, extract just that one:
   308	
   309	```bash
   310	unzip -p /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.zip path/inside/file.txt
   311	```
   312	
   313	**Standalone `.gz`** (not a tar) compresses a single file — there is
   314	no manifest to list. Just peek at the decompressed content:
   315	
   316	```bash
   317	zcat /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json.gz | head -50
   318	```
   319	
   320	---
   321	
   322	## EPUB / ODT
   323	
   324	```bash
   325	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/book.epub | head -200
   326	```
   327	
   328	For long ebooks, pipe through `head` — you rarely need the whole thing
   329	to answer a question.
   330	
   331	---
   332	
   333	## RTF / IPYNB
   334	
   335	```bash
   336	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/notes.rtf | head -200
   337	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/notebook.ipynb | head -200
   338	```
   339	
   340	---
   341	
   342	## Plain text / code / logs
   343	
   344	Check the size first:
   345	
   346	```bash
   347	wc -c /mnt/user-data/uploads/app.log
   348	```
   349	
   350	- **Under ~20KB**: `cat` is fine.
   351	- **Over ~20KB**: `head -100` and `tail -100` to orient. If the user
   352	  asked about something specific, `grep` for it. Load the whole thing
   353	  only if you genuinely need all of it.
   354	
   355	For log files, the user almost always cares about the end:
   356	
   357	```bash
   358	tail -200 /mnt/user-data/uploads/app.log
   359	```
   360	
   361	---
   362	
   363	## Unknown extension
   364	
   365	```bash
   366	file /mnt/user-data/uploads/mystery.bin
   367	xxd /mnt/user-data/uploads/mystery.bin | head -5
   368	```
   369	
   370	`file` identifies most things. `xxd` head shows magic bytes. If `file`
   371	says "data" and the hex doesn't match anything you recognize, ask the
   372	user what it is instead of guessing.
   373

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"# CN Synthetic Collections Data 

 collections data for three problem statements. Everything in it is invented.

## Files

| File | What it holds | Used for |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `data/shared/accounts.csv` | One row per loan account: lender, product, bucket, dues and what the lender knows about the borrower | PS1, PS2, Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/shared/splits.csv` | Which accounts are train, validation and test | PS1, PS2, Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/shared/lenders.csv` | The six lenders | PS1, PS2, Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/shared/agents.csv` | Tele-calling agents, field agents and the voice bot | PS1, PS2, Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/shared/dial_attempts.csv` | Every outbound call attempt, with its result, disposition and agent remark | PS1, PS2 |
| `data/shared/payments.csv` | Every payment received | PS1, PS2 |
| `data/shared/addresses.csv` | Every address on file, as written in the lender's system | PS2, Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/shared/field_visits.csv` | Every field visit, with check-in location, outcome and agent remark | PS2, Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/ps1_fake_ptp/ptps.csv` | Every promise to pay recorded on a call or a visit | PS1 |
| `data/ps1_fake_ptp/call_transcripts.csv` | Turn-by-turn transcripts of calls | PS1 |
| `data/ps1_fake_ptp/post_call_events.csv` | What happened after a PTP: payment link sent or opened, WhatsApp confirmations, customer calls | PS1 |
| `data/ps1_fake_ptp/annotated_ptp_sample.csv` | 200 PTPs labelled by type by a reviewer (some labels are wrong) | PS1 |
| `data/ps2_right_party_contact/phones.csv` | Every phone number linked to an account, and where the number came from | PS2 |
| `data/ps2_right_party_contact/skip_traces.csv` | Skip-trace requests and what they found | PS2 |
| `data/ps2_right_party_contact/verified_contact_points.csv` | 250 numbers checked by a verification campaign | PS2 |
| `data/address_geocoder/towns.csv` | The three towns | Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/address_geocoder/localities.csv` | Localities in each town, with pincode and approximate centre | Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/address_geocoder/landmarks_poi.csv` | Landmark database (incomplete and slightly off) | Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/address_geocoder/baseline_geocodes.csv` | Where a commercial geocoder places each address: the baseline to beat | Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/address_geocoder/visit_gps_points.csv` | GPS trail for each field visit | Geocoding_Engine |
| `data/address_geocoder/surveyed_addresses.csv` | 100 addresses with accurately surveyed locations | Geocoding_Engine |

## Files by problem statement

PS1, Real-Time Fake PTP Detection: `ptps.csv`, `call_transcripts.csv`, `post_call_events.csv`, `annotated_ptp_sample.csv`, `dial_attempts.csv`, `payments.csv`, `accounts.csv`, `agents.csv`

PS2, Right-Party Contact Prediction and Skip-Trace Prioritisation: `dial_attempts.csv`, `phones.csv`, `skip_traces.csv`, `verified_contact_points.csv`, `field_visits.csv`, `addresses.csv`, `payments.csv`, `accounts.csv`, `agents.csv`

Geocoding_Engine, Address Geocoder That Learns from Field Visits: `addresses.csv`, `baseline_geocodes.csv`, `field_visits.csv`, `visit_gps_points.csv`, `surveyed_addresses.csv`, `localities.csv`, `landmarks_poi.csv`, `towns.csv`, `accounts.csv`, `agents.csv`

All three also use `splits.csv`.

cd /home/claude/work/Dataset/data && python3 - <<'EOF'
import pandas as pd, glob, os
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_columns',60); pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth',60)
for f in sorted(glob.glob('address_geocoder/*.csv')+glob.glob('shared/*.csv')):
    if 'dial_attempts' in f: 
        df=pd.read_csv(f,nrows=3); print('\n=====',f,'(skipped full load; head only)'); print(df); continue
    df=pd.read_csv(f)
    print('\n=====',f,df.shape)
    print(df.dtypes.to_string())
    print(df.head(3).to_string())
    nn=df.isna().sum(); print('NULLS:',nn[nn>0].to_dict())
EOF

cd /home/claude/work/Dataset/data && python3 - <<'EOF'
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_columns',60); pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth',100)
A=pd.read_csv('shared/addresses.csv'); V=pd.read_csv('shared/field_visits.csv'); B=pd.read_csv('address_geocoder/baseline_geocodes.csv')
S=pd.read_csv('address_geocoder/surveyed_addresses.csv'); L=pd.read_csv('address_geocoder/localities.csv'); P=pd.read_csv('address_geocoder/landmarks_poi.csv')
acc=pd.read_csv('shared/accounts.csv'); sp=pd.read_csv('shared/splits.csv'); ag=pd.read_csv('shared/agents.csv'); le=pd.read_csv('shared/lenders.csv')
print(le.to_string()); print(ag.to_string())
print('\n--- addresses'); 
for c in ['address_type','source','town_id']: print(A[c].value_counts().to_dict())
print('dup address_text:',A.address_text.duplicated().sum(),' unique accts:',A.account_id.nunique())
print('added_date range',A.added_date.min(),A.added_date.max())
print(A.groupby('account_id').size().value_counts().to_dict())
print('\nSample addr text by town/lender:')
A=A.merge(acc[['account_id','lender_id','preferred_language']],on='account_id')
for (t,l),g in A.groupby(['town_id','lender_id']):
    print(t,l,'|',' || '.join(g.address_text.sample(2,random_state=1)))
print('\n--- baseline'); print(B.precision.value_counts().to_dict()); print(B.describe().to_string())
print('baseline ids in addresses:',B.address_id.isin(A.address_id).mean(),' addresses w/o baseline:',(~A.address_id.isin(B.address_id)).sum())
print('\n--- visits'); print(V.outcome.value_counts().to_string()); print(V.describe().to_string())
print('visit dates',V.visit_date.min(),V.visit_date.max(),' n agents',V.agent_id.nunique())
print('visits per address:',V.groupby('address_id').size().value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
print('addresses with >=1 visit:',V.address_id.nunique(),'/',len(A))
print('\n--- splits'); print(sp.split.value_counts().to_dict())
print('\n--- surveyed in splits:'); print(S.merge(A[['address_id','account_id','town_id']],on='address_id').merge(sp,on='account_id').groupby(['town_id','split']).size())
print('\n--- landmarks'); print(P.groupby('town_id').size().to_dict()); print(P.landmark_type.value_counts().to_dict()); print(P.name.value_counts().head(15).to_dict())
print('\n--- localities'); print(L.to_string())
EOF

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_columns',60); pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth',90)
A=pd.read_csv('shared/addresses.csv'); V=pd.read_csv('shared/field_visits.csv'); B=pd.read_csv('address_geocoder/baseline_geocodes.csv')
S=pd.read_csv('address_geocoder/surveyed_addresses.csv'); acc=pd.read_csv('shared/accounts.csv'); sp=pd.read_csv('shared/splits.csv')
A=A.merge(acc[['account_id','lender_id','portfolio','preferred_language']],on='account_id').merge(sp,on='account_id')
# baseline vs truth
T=S.merge(B,on='address_id').merge(A,on='address_id')
T['err']=np.hypot(T.geocoder_x-T.surveyed_x,T.geocoder_y-T.surveyed_y)
print('BASELINE error on 100 surveyed: median %.0f p90 %.0f mean %.0f'%(T.err.median(),T.err.quantile(.9),T.err.mean()))
print(T.groupby('precision').err.describe().round(0))
print(T.groupby('town_id').err.describe().round(0))
print(T.groupby('lender_id').err.describe().round(0))
# surveyed addr with visits
V=V.merge(A[['address_id','town_id','lender_id','split']],on='address_id')
VS=V.merge(S,on='address_id'); VS['d']=np.hypot(VS.checkin_x-VS.surveyed_x,VS.checkin_y-VS.surveyed_y)
print('\nvisits on surveyed addrs:',len(VS),' addrs:',VS.address_id.nunique())
print(VS.groupby('outcome').d.describe().round(0))
print(VS.groupby('agent_id').d.describe().round(0))
# lag, dwell
for c in ['start_ts','checkin_ts']: V[c]=pd.to_datetime(V[c])
V['lag_min']=(V.checkin_ts-V.start_ts).dt.total_seconds()/60
print('\nlag min',V.lag_min.describe().round(1).to_dict())
print(V.groupby('outcome')[['dwell_s','gps_accuracy_m','lag_min']].median().round(1))
print(V.groupby('agent_id').agg(n=('visit_id','size'),dw=('dwell_s','median'),acc=('gps_accuracy_m','median'),lag=('lag_min','median'),
   met=('outcome',lambda s:(s.isin(['met_borrower','cash_collected'])).mean().round(2)),nt=('outcome',lambda s:(s=='address_not_traceable').mean().round(2)),
   dup_photo=('photo_hash',lambda s:s.duplicated(keep=False).mean().round(3)),town=('town_id',lambda s:s.value_counts().index[0])))
print('\nphoto_hash dup overall:',V.photo_hash.duplicated(keep=False).sum(), ' null:',V.photo_hash.isna().sum())
print('visits w/ OUT addr:',(V.town_id=='OUT').sum())
print('visits per day per agent:',V.groupby(['agent_id','visit_date']).size().describe().round(1).to_dict())
print('town mismatch agent vs addr town (excluding OUT):')
ag=pd.read_csv('shared/agents.csv'); print(V.merge(ag[['agent_id','town_id']].rename(columns={'town_id':'ag_town'}),on='agent_id').groupby(['ag_town','town_id']).size().unstack(fill_value=0))
EOF

nt=VS[(VS.outcome=='address_not_traceable')]; print('\nnot traceable on surveyed:',len(nt),' hot share',nt.hot.mean().round(2)); print(nt.d.describe().round(0))

cd /home/claude/work/Dataset/data && python3 -c "
import importlib
for m in ['rapidfuzz','sklearn','scipy','lightgbm','xgboost','matplotlib','seaborn','statsmodels','torch','shapely','pyproj','unidecode','indic_transliteration']:
    try: importlib.import_module(m); print(m,'OK')
    except Exception as e: print(m,'MISSING')
"
python3 - <<'EOF'
import pandas as pd, re, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth',140)
A=pd.read_csv('shared/addresses.csv'); V=pd.read_csv('shared/field_visits.csv')
# token inventory for script / landmark words
import collections
tok=collections.Counter()
for t in A.address_text: tok.update(re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+",t.lower()))
print(len(tok)); print(tok.most_common(130))
print('\nnon-ascii addresses:',A.address_text.str.contains(r'[^\x00-\x7F]').mean().round(3))
print(A[A.address_text.str.contains(r'[\u0C80-\u0CFF]')].address_text.head(5).tolist())
print(A[A.address_text.str.contains(r'[\u0900-\u097F]')].address_text.head(5).tolist())
print('\nA.address_type=native vs OUT:',pd.crosstab(A.address_type,A.town_id))
print('src skip_trace sample:'); print(A[A.source=='skip_trace'].head(6).to_string())
print('\nremarks top:'); print(V.remark.value_counts().head(40).to_string())
print('\nremarks w/ location correction words:')
m=V[V.remark.str.contains(r'actual|nija|asli|sahi|aage|peeche|hinde|munde|gali|lane|opposite|behind|ahead|beside|road',case=False,regex=True)]
print(len(m)); print(m.remark.sample(25,random_state=2).to_string())
EOF

import re, difflib, numpy as np, pandas as pd

    return s
# landmark lexicon -> canonical type (English, Kannada, Hindi variants)
LEX={'ration_shop':['ration shop','ration ki dukaan','pds shop','pds','ನ್ಯಾಯಬೆಲೆ ಅಂಗಡಿ','राशन की दुकान','fair price shop'],
 'bus_stop':['bus stop','bus stand','bus nildana','ಬಸ್ ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ','बस स्टॉप','बस स्टैंड'],
 'govt_school':['govt school','government school','sarkari school','ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಶಾಲೆ','सरकारी स्कूल'],
 'masjid':['masjid','mosque','मस्जिद','ಮಸೀದಿ'],
 'hanuman_temple':['hanuman temple','hanuman mandir','ಹನುಮಾನ್ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನ','हनुमान मंदिर','anjaneya temple'],
 'medical_store':['medical store','medicals','pharmacy','medical shop','dawai ki dukaan','ಮೆಡಿಕಲ್','मेडिकल','दवाई की दुकान'],
 'ganesha_temple':['ganesh temple','ganapathi gudi','ganapathi temple','ಗಣಪತಿ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನ','गणेश मंदिर','ganesha temple'],
 'water_tank':['water tank','paani ki tanki','ನೀರಿನ ಟ್ಯಾಂಕ್','पानी की टंकी'],
 'milk_dairy':['milk dairy','doodh dairy','ಹಾಲಿನ ಡೈರಿ','दूध डेयरी','dairy'],
 'community_hall':['community hall','kalyana mantapa','kalyna mantapa','ಕಲ್ಯಾಣ ಮಂಟಪ','barat ghar','कम्युनिटी हॉल','बारात घर'],
 'park':['park','ಉದ್ಯಾನ','पार्क'],
 'church':['church','ಚರ್ಚ್','चर्च'],
 'post_office':['post office','anche kacheri','dak ghar','ಅಂಚೆ ಕಚೇರಿ','डाकघर'],
 'petrol_bunk':['petrol bunk','petrol pump','petrol puump','ಪೆಟ್ರೋಲ್ ಬಂಕ್','पेट्रोल पंप']}
REL={'near':['near','nr','close to','hattira','ke paas','ke pass','paas','ಹತ್ತಿರ','के पास','beside','ಪಕ್ಕ','के बगल में','bagal'],
 'behind':['behind','b/h','bhd','ke peeche','ಹಿಂದೆ','के पीछे','hinde'],
 'opp':['opposite','opp','opp.','ke saamne','ಎದುರು','के सामने','eduru']}
def locality_match(text,town):
    t=norm(text); sub=LOC[LOC.town_id==town]; best=(None,0)
    for _,r in sub.iterrows():
        n=norm(r.locality_name); 
        if n in t: sc=1.0
        else:
            toks=re.findall(r'[a-z0-9]+',t); k=len(n.split()); sc=0
            for i in range(len(toks)-k+1):
                sc=max(sc,difflib.SequenceMatcher(None,n,' '.join(toks[i:i+k])).ratio())
        if sc>best[1]: best=(r.locality_id,sc)
    return best
def parse(text,town):
    t=text.lower(); o={}
    lm,sc=locality_match(text,town) if town!='OUT' else (None,0); o['loc_id']=lm if sc>=0.8 else None; o['loc_score']=sc
    m=re.search(r'(\d{5,6})\s*$',t); o['pin_text']=int(m.group(1)) if m else None
    nn=norm(t)
    c=re.search(r'(\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s*(?:cross|crs|cr|x)\b',nn); o['cross']=int(c.group(1)) if c else None
    c=re.search(r'(\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s*(?:main|mn)\b',nn); o['main']=int(c.group(1)) if c else None
    c=re.search(r'gali(?:\s*no\.?)?[-\s]*(\d+)|गली नं\.?\s*(\d+)',nn); o['gali']=int([g for g in c.groups() if g][0]) if c else None
    c=re.search(r'ward\s*(\d+)',nn); o['ward']=int(c.group(1)) if c else None
    c=re.search(r'\b([a-f])\s*(?:block|blk)\b|\b(?:block|blk)\.?\s*([a-f])\b',nn); o['block']=(c.group(1) or c.group(2)).upper() if c else None
    c=re.search(r'(\d+)(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\s*(?:road|rd)\b|\b(?:road|rd)\s*(\d+)',nn); o['road']=int([g for g in c.groups() if g][0]) if c else None
    lt=None
    for typ,ws in LEX.items():
        for w in sorted(ws,key=len,reverse=True):
            if w in t: lt=typ;break
        if lt: break
    o['lm_type']=lt
    o['rel']=next((r for r,ws in REL.items() if any(re.search(r'(?<!\w)'+re.escape(w)+r'(?!\w)',t) for w in ws)),None) if lt else None
    return o

def gmed(p,it=30):
    m=p.mean(0)
    for _ in range(it):
        d=np.maximum(np.hypot(*(p-m).T),1e-3); w=1/d; m=(p*w[:,None]).sum(0)/w.sum()
    return m
C=pd.DataFrame([(a,*gmed(g[['checkin_x','checkin_y']].values)) for a,g in good.groupby('address_id')],columns=['address_id','cx','cy'])

def cr(df,k,t):
    r=[(abs(np.corrcoef(g[k],g[t])[0,1])) for _,g in df.groupby('loc_id') if len(g)>8 and g[k].nunique()>2]; return np.nanmean(r) if r else np.nan
t2=M[(M.town_id=='T2')&M.gali.notna()]; print('T2 gali corr dx %.2f dy %.2f | ward dx %.2f dy %.2f'%(cr(t2,'gali','dx'),cr(t2,'gali','dy'),cr(M[(M.town_id=='T2')&M.ward.notna()],'ward','dx'),cr(M[(M.town_id=='T2')&M.ward.notna()],'ward','dy')))
t3=M[(M.town_id=='T3')]; t3=t3.assign(bl=t3.block.map(lambda b:ord(b)-65 if isinstance(b,str) else np.nan))
print('T3 block corr dx %.2f dy %.2f | road dx %.2f dy %.2f'%(cr(t3.dropna(subset=['bl']),'bl','dx'),cr(t3.dropna(subset=['bl']),'bl','dy'),cr(t3.dropna(subset=['road']),'road','dx'),cr(t3.dropna(subset=['road']),'road','dy')))

    bx=np.linalg.lstsq(X,g.dx,rcond=None)[0]; by=np.linalg.lstsq(X,g.dy,rcond=None)[0]
    r=np.hypot(g.dx-X@bx,g.dy-X@by); res.append((lid,len(g),bx[1],by[2],r.median(),np.hypot(g.dx,g.dy).median()))

R=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=['best_possible','nearest_to_locality','dist_poi_to_locctr','npoi']); print('\nlandmark lookup (n=%d): nearest POI of that type to locality centroid -> truth: median %.0f p75 %.0f ; oracle best POI -> truth median %.0f'%(len(R),R.nearest_to_locality.median(),R.nearest_to_locality.quantile(.75),R.best_possible.median()))
print(R.describe().round(0))
print('\nPOI per locality per type (avg count of same-type POI within 700 m of centroid):')
print(P.groupby(['town_id','landmark_type']).size().unstack(0).fillna(0).astype(int).to_string())

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, re, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
pd.set_option('display.width',250); pd.set_option('display.max_colwidth',110)
D='/home/claude/work/Dataset/data/'
A=pd.read_pickle('/home/claude/work/addr_parsed.pkl'); V=pd.read_csv(D+'shared/field_visits.csv'); S=pd.read_csv(D+'address_geocoder/surveyed_addresses.csv')
def hn(t):
    m=re.search(r'(?:no\.?|house|h\.?no\.?|#)\s*(\d+(?:/\d+)?)',t.lower()) or re.match(r'\s*(\d+(?:/\d+)?)[, ]',t)
    return m.group(1) if m else None
A['house']=A.address_text.map(hn)
g=A[(A.town_id!='OUT')&A.house.notna()].copy()
gc=g[['cross','main','gali','ward','block','road']].astype(str)
g['key']=g.town_id+'|'+g.loc_id.fillna('?').astype(str)+'|'+gc.apply(lambda r:'/'.join(r),axis=1)+'|'+g.house.astype(str)
k=g.groupby('key').size(); print('keys with >1 address:',(k>1).sum(),' addresses involved:',k[k>1].sum(),' of',len(g))
print(g[g.key.isin(k[k>1].index)].sort_values('key')[['address_id','account_id','source','address_type','address_text']].head(14).to_string())
k2=g.groupby(['town_id','loc_id','house']).size(); print('loose (loc+house) groups >1:',(k2>1).sum(),'rows',k2[k2>1].sum())
print('address-type combos per account:',A.groupby('account_id').address_type.apply(lambda s:'|'.join(sorted(s))).value_counts().head(6).to_dict())
Vx=V.merge(A[['address_id','address_type','source']],on='address_id'); print(Vx.address_type.value_counts().to_dict(),Vx.source.value_counts().to_dict())
st=A[A.source=='skip_trace'].address_id; print('skip-trace addrs visited:',V.address_id.isin(st).sum(),'of',len(st))
print('surveyed addr types:',S.merge(A,on='address_id').address_type.value_counts().to_dict())
V['start_ts']=pd.to_datetime(V.start_ts); V=V.sort_values(['address_id','start_ts']); V['k']=V.groupby('address_id').cumcount()
print('not-traceable rate by visit index:',V.groupby('k').outcome.apply(lambda s:(s=='address_not_traceable').mean()).round(2).to_dict())
# repeat structure: after a found visit, are there still not-traceable visits for same address?
f=V.groupby('address_id').outcome.apply(lambda s:((s!='address_not_traceable').any(),(s=='address_not_traceable').any())); 
print('addresses with both found and not-traceable visits:',sum(1 for a,b in f if a and b),' only NT:',sum(1 for a,b in f if (not a) and b),' only found:',sum(1 for a,b in f if a and not b))
EOF

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
pd.set_option('display.width',250)
D='/home/claude/work/Dataset/data/'
V=pd.read_csv(D+'shared/field_visits.csv'); B=pd.read_csv(D+'address_geocoder/baseline_geocodes.csv'); S=pd.read_csv(D+'address_geocoder/surveyed_addresses.csv'); G=pd.read_csv(D+'address_geocoder/visit_gps_points.csv')
M=V.merge(B,on='address_id',how='left'); M['d_base']=np.hypot(M.checkin_x-M.geocoder_x,M.checkin_y-M.geocoder_y)
print('visit check-in distance to baseline pin by outcome (m):'); print(M.groupby('outcome').d_base.describe()[['count','25%','50%','75%']].round(0))
ms=M.merge(S,on='address_id'); ms['d_truth']=np.hypot(ms.checkin_x-ms.surveyed_x,ms.checkin_y-ms.surveyed_y); ms['b_err']=np.hypot(ms.geocoder_x-ms.surveyed_x,ms.geocoder_y-ms.surveyed_y)
nt=ms[ms.outcome=='address_not_traceable']; print('\nNT visits on surveyed: corr(d_truth, baseline error)= %.2f ; median d_base %.0f ; median baseline err %.0f'%(np.corrcoef(nt.d_truth,nt.b_err)[0,1],nt.d_base.median(),nt.b_err.median()))
# baseline error vs probability of NT, using surveyed visits
ms['nt']=ms.outcome=='address_not_traceable'; ms['hot']=False
x=ms[ms.agent_id!='FA009']; print(x.groupby(pd.cut(x.b_err,[0,50,100,200,400,800,5000])).nt.agg(['mean','count']).round(2))
# how far is NT trail from the truth: min distance of any trail point to truth
Gs=G.merge(nt[['visit_id','surveyed_x','surveyed_y']],on='visit_id'); Gs['d']=np.hypot(Gs.x-Gs.surveyed_x,Gs.y-Gs.surveyed_y)
mind=Gs.groupby('visit_id').d.min(); print('\nNT trails: min dist of any trail point to true house — median %.0f, p25 %.0f, share passing within 50 m: %.2f, within 100 m: %.2f'%(mind.median(),mind.quantile(.25),(mind<50).mean(),(mind<100).mean()))
# same for found visits' pre-checkin trail (agent walking in from afar)
print('NT start->checkin: agent travels? disp of trail first->last median:',end=' ')
g=G.sort_values(['visit_id','seq']); f=g.groupby('visit_id').first(); l=g.groupby('visit_id').last(); disp=np.hypot(l.x-f.x,l.y-f.y); vid=nt.visit_id; print(disp.loc[vid.values].median().round(0))
EOF

"""Bayesian grid geocoder: text prior (locality + street grid) x landmark factor x baseline obs x robust visit evidence."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from data import *

GRID = {'T1': ['main', 'cross'], 'T2': ['gali'], 'T3': ['blk_idx', 'road']}
PIN2LOC = LOC.groupby(['town_id', 'pincode']).locality_id.apply(list).to_dict()
LOCR = LOC.set_index('locality_id')
AREA = np.pi * 4500.0 ** 2

# ---------- robust consensus ----------
def gmedian(p, w=None, it=40):
    w = np.ones(len(p)) if w is None else np.asarray(w, float)
    m = (p * w[:, None]).sum(0) / w.sum()
    for _ in range(it):
        d = np.maximum(np.hypot(*(p - m).T), 1e-2); ww = w / d; m = (p * ww[:, None]).sum(0) / ww.sum()
    return m

def consensus_labels(V, bad_agents=()):
    g = V[V.found & ~V.f_hard & ~V.agent_id.isin(bad_agents)]
    rows = [(a, *gmedian(x[['tx', 'ty']].values), len(x)) for a, x in g.groupby('address_id')]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['address_id', 'lx', 'ly', 'n_lab'])

# ---------- text prior ----------
class TextPrior:
    def fit(self, A, lab):
        d = A.merge(lab, on='address_id'); d = d[d.loc_id.notna()]
        self.slope, self.fm, self.icpt, self.sig = {}, {}, {}, {}
        for t, cols in GRID.items():
            s = d[d.town_id == t].copy()
            L0 = LOCR[LOCR.town_id == t]
            for c in cols: self.fm[(t, c)] = s.groupby('loc_id')[c].mean().to_dict(); 
            def dm(r):  # locality-demeaned grid fields (missing -> 0)
                return np.array([(r[c] - self.fm[(t, c)].get(r.loc_id, np.nanmean(list(self.fm[(t, c)].values())))) if pd.notna(r[c]) else 0.0 for c in cols])
            F = np.vstack([dm(r) for _, r in s.iterrows()]) if len(s) else np.zeros((0, len(cols)))
            full = np.array([all(pd.notna(r[c]) for c in cols) for _, r in s.iterrows()])
            cx = LOCR.loc[s.loc_id, 'centroid_x'].values; cy = LOCR.loc[s.loc_id, 'centroid_y'].values
            dx, dy = (s.lx.values - cx), (s.ly.values - cy)
            dxm = dx - pd.Series(dx).groupby(s.loc_id.values).transform('median').values
            dym = dy - pd.Series(dy).groupby(s.loc_id.values).transform('median').values
            B = np.zeros((len(cols), 2))
            for j, y in enumerate([dxm, dym]):
                Xf, yf = F[full], y[full]; w = np.ones(len(yf))
                for _ in range(20):
                    b = np.linalg.lstsq(Xf * np.sqrt(w)[:, None], yf * np.sqrt(w), rcond=None)[0]
                    r = yf - Xf @ b; sc = max(1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(r)), 10); w = 1 / np.maximum(1, np.abs(r) / (1.5 * sc))
                B[:, j] = b
            self.slope[t] = B
            res_x = dx - F @ B[:, 0]; res_y = dy - F @ B[:, 1]
            off_x, off_y = np.median(res_x), np.median(res_y)
            for lid in L0.locality_id:
                m = (s.loc_id.values == lid)
                k = 3.0
                px = (np.median(res_x[m]) * m.sum() + off_x * k) / (m.sum() + k) if m.any() else off_x
                py = (np.median(res_y[m]) * m.sum() + off_y * k) / (m.sum() + k) if m.any() else off_y
                self.icpt[lid] = (LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_x'] + px, LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_y'] + py)
            # residual sigma by availability pattern
            rx = res_x - np.array([self.icpt[l][0] - LOCR.loc[l, 'centroid_x'] for l in s.loc_id]); ry = res_y - np.array([self.icpt[l][1] - LOCR.loc[l, 'centroid_y'] for l in s.loc_id])
            pat = np.array([''.join('1' if pd.notna(r[c]) else '0' for c in cols) for _, r in s.iterrows()])
            for p in set(pat):
                m = pat == p
                sx = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(rx[m] - np.median(rx[m])))) if m.sum() >= 8 else None
                sy = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(ry[m] - np.median(ry[m])))) if m.sum() >= 8 else None
                self.sig[(t, p)] = (sx, sy)
            allsx = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(rx - np.median(rx)))); allsy = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(ry - np.median(ry))))
            self.sig[(t, 'all')] = (allsx, allsy)
        return self

    def components(self, r, mode='grid'):
        """Return list of (weight, mu(2), sig(2)) for an address row; [] if none."""
        t = r.town_id
        if t not in GRID: return []
        cols = GRID[t]
        if pd.notna(r.loc_id): cand = [(r.loc_id, 1.0)]
        else:
            pins = PIN2LOC.get((t, r.pin_text))
            ids = pins if pins else list(LOC[LOC.town_id == t].locality_id)
            cand = [(i, 1.0 / len(ids)) for i in ids]
        out = []
        pat = ''.join('1' if pd.notna(r[c]) else '0' for c in cols)
        sx, sy = self.sig.get((t, pat)) or (None, None)
        if sx is None: sx, sy = self.sig[(t, 'all')]
        for lid, w in cand:
            mu = np.array(self.icpt[lid], float)
            if mode == 'centroid': mu = np.array([LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_x'], LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_y']])
            elif mode == 'icpt': pass
            else:
                B = self.slope[t]
                for k, c in enumerate(cols):
                    if pd.notna(r[c]):
                        mu = mu + (r[c] - self.fm[(t, c)].get(lid, r[c])) * B[k]
            sg = (sx, sy) if mode == 'grid' else (max(sx, 250.0), max(sy, 250.0)) if mode == 'icpt' else (450.0, 450.0)
            out.append((w, mu, np.array(sg)))
        return out

# ---------- landmark factor ----------
POIT = {(t, k): g[['x', 'y']].values for (t, k), g in POI.groupby(['town_id', 'landmark_type'])}
def lm_factor(X, Y, town, ltype, sig, eps):
    P = POIT.get((town, ltype))
    if P is None: return 1.0
    miss = np.ones_like(X)
    for px, py in P:
        miss *= 1 - np.exp(-((X - px) ** 2 + (Y - py) ** 2) / (2 * sig ** 2))
    return eps + (1 - eps) * (1 - miss)

BASE_SIG = {'rooftop': 30.0, 'street': 120.0, 'locality': 500.0, 'pincode': 2000.0}

def posterior(r, prior, vis, cfg, trails=None):
    """vis: DataFrame of this address's visits (already with rho, s). Returns dict with pin, radius, etc. or None."""
    comps = prior.components(r, cfg.get('prior', 'grid')) if cfg.get('prior', 'grid') != 'none' else []
    anchors = [c[1] for c in comps]
    base = None
    if pd.notna(r.geocoder_x) and (cfg.get('use_base', True) or not comps): base = np.array([r.geocoder_x, r.geocoder_y]); anchors.append(base)
    vm = vis[vis.use] if len(vis) else vis
    if len(vm): anchors += [np.array([a, b]) for a, b in zip(vm.ex, vm.ey)]
    if not anchors: return None
    An = np.array(anchors)
    pad = 450.0
    lo, hi = An.min(0) - pad, An.max(0) + pad
    side = max(hi - lo)
    if side > 5200:  # cap: keep window around main modes
        c = np.median(An, 0); lo, hi = c - 2600, c + 2600; side = 5200
    res = max(8.0, side / 330)
    xs = np.arange(lo[0], hi[0], res); ys = np.arange(lo[1], hi[1], res)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    lp = np.zeros_like(X)
    if comps:
        dens = np.zeros_like(X)
        for w, mu, sg in comps:
            dens += w * np.exp(-0.5 * (((X - mu[0]) / sg[0]) ** 2 + ((Y - mu[1]) / sg[1]) ** 2)) / (2 * np.pi * sg[0] * sg[1])
        if cfg.get('use_poi', True) and r.lm_type and pd.notna(r.lm_type):
            dens = dens * lm_factor(X, Y, r.town_id, r.lm_type, cfg['lm_sig'], cfg['lm_eps'])
        lp += np.log(dens + 1e-14)
    if base is not None and cfg.get('use_base', True):
        sb = BASE_SIG.get(r.precision, 500.0); ob = 0.15
        lp += np.log((1 - ob) * np.exp(-((X - base[0]) ** 2 + (Y - base[1]) ** 2) / (2 * sb ** 2)) / (2 * np.pi * sb ** 2) + ob / AREA)
    vmode = cfg.get('visits', 'robust')
    if vmode != 'none' and len(vm):
        for _, v in vm.iterrows():
            s = v.s; d2 = (X - v.ex) ** 2 + (Y - v.ey) ** 2
            lp += np.log((1 - v.rho) * np.exp(-d2 / (2 * s * s)) / (2 * np.pi * s * s) + v.rho / AREA)
    if cfg.get('use_neg', False) and len(vis):
        nt = vis[~vis.found & ~vis.f_hard]
        for _, v in nt.iterrows():
            tx, ty = trails[v.visit_id]
            dmin = np.full_like(X, 1e9)
            for px, py in zip(tx, ty): dmin = np.minimum(dmin, (X - px) ** 2 + (Y - py) ** 2)
            lp += np.log(1 - cfg['neg_q'] * np.exp(-dmin / (2 * cfg['neg_s'] ** 2)))

"""Bayesian grid geocoder: text prior (locality + street grid) x landmark factor x baseline obs x robust visit evidence."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from data import *

GRID = {'T1': ['main', 'cross'], 'T2': ['gali'], 'T3': ['blk_idx', 'road']}
PIN2LOC = LOC.groupby(['town_id', 'pincode']).locality_id.apply(list).to_dict()
LOCR = LOC.set_index('locality_id')
AREA = np.pi * 4500.0 ** 2

# ---------- robust consensus ----------
def gmedian(p, w=None, it=40):
    w = np.ones(len(p)) if w is None else np.asarray(w, float)
    m = (p * w[:, None]).sum(0) / w.sum()
    for _ in range(it):
        d = np.maximum(np.hypot(*(p - m).T), 1e-2); ww = w / d; m = (p * ww[:, None]).sum(0) / ww.sum()
    return m

def consensus_labels(V, bad_agents=()):
    g = V[V.found & ~V.f_hard & ~V.agent_id.isin(bad_agents)]
    rows = [(a, *gmedian(x[['tx', 'ty']].values), len(x)) for a, x in g.groupby('address_id')]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['address_id', 'lx', 'ly', 'n_lab'])

# ---------- text prior ----------
class TextPrior:
    def fit(self, A, lab):
        d = A.merge(lab, on='address_id'); d = d[d.loc_id.notna()]
        self.slope, self.fm, self.icpt, self.sig = {}, {}, {}, {}
        for t, cols in GRID.items():
            s = d[d.town_id == t].copy()
            L0 = LOCR[LOCR.town_id == t]
            for c in cols: self.fm[(t, c)] = s.groupby('loc_id')[c].mean().to_dict(); 
            def dm(r):  # locality-demeaned grid fields (missing -> 0)
                return np.array([(r[c] - self.fm[(t, c)].get(r.loc_id, np.nanmean(list(self.fm[(t, c)].values())))) if pd.notna(r[c]) else 0.0 for c in cols])
            F = np.vstack([dm(r) for _, r in s.iterrows()]) if len(s) else np.zeros((0, len(cols)))
            full = np.array([all(pd.notna(r[c]) for c in cols) for _, r in s.iterrows()])
            cx = LOCR.loc[s.loc_id, 'centroid_x'].values; cy = LOCR.loc[s.loc_id, 'centroid_y'].values
            dx, dy = (s.lx.values - cx), (s.ly.values - cy)
            dxm = dx - pd.Series(dx).groupby(s.loc_id.values).transform('median').values
            dym = dy - pd.Series(dy).groupby(s.loc_id.values).transform('median').values
            B = np.zeros((len(cols), 2))
            for j, y in enumerate([dxm, dym]):
                Xf, yf = F[full], y[full]; w = np.ones(len(yf))
                for _ in range(20):
                    b = np.linalg.lstsq(Xf * np.sqrt(w)[:, None], yf * np.sqrt(w), rcond=None)[0]
                    r = yf - Xf @ b; sc = max(1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(r)), 10); w = 1 / np.maximum(1, np.abs(r) / (1.5 * sc))
                B[:, j] = b
            self.slope[t] = B
            res_x = dx - F @ B[:, 0]; res_y = dy - F @ B[:, 1]
            off_x, off_y = np.median(res_x), np.median(res_y)
            for lid in L0.locality_id:
                m = (s.loc_id.values == lid)
                k = 3.0
                px = (np.median(res_x[m]) * m.sum() + off_x * k) / (m.sum() + k) if m.any() else off_x
                py = (np.median(res_y[m]) * m.sum() + off_y * k) / (m.sum() + k) if m.any() else off_y
                self.icpt[lid] = (LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_x'] + px, LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_y'] + py)
            # residual sigma by availability pattern
            rx = res_x - np.array([self.icpt[l][0] - LOCR.loc[l, 'centroid_x'] for l in s.loc_id]); ry = res_y - np.array([self.icpt[l][1] - LOCR.loc[l, 'centroid_y'] for l in s.loc_id])
            pat = np.array([''.join('1' if pd.notna(r[c]) else '0' for c in cols) for _, r in s.iterrows()])
            for p in set(pat):
                m = pat == p
                sx = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(rx[m] - np.median(rx[m])))) if m.sum() >= 8 else None
                sy = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(ry[m] - np.median(ry[m])))) if m.sum() >= 8 else None
                self.sig[(t, p)] = (sx, sy)
            allsx = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(rx - np.median(rx)))); allsy = max(35.0, 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(ry - np.median(ry))))
            self.sig[(t, 'all')] = (allsx, allsy)
        return self

    def components(self, r, mode='grid'):
        """Return list of (weight, mu(2), sig(2)) for an address row; [] if none."""
        t = r.town_id
        if t not in GRID: return []
        cols = GRID[t]
        if pd.notna(r.loc_id): cand = [(r.loc_id, 1.0)]
        else:
            pins = PIN2LOC.get((t, r.pin_text))
            ids = pins if pins else list(LOC[LOC.town_id == t].locality_id)
            cand = [(i, 1.0 / len(ids)) for i in ids]
        out = []
        pat = ''.join('1' if pd.notna(r[c]) else '0' for c in cols)
        sx, sy = self.sig.get((t, pat)) or (None, None)
        if sx is None: sx, sy = self.sig[(t, 'all')]
        for lid, w in cand:
            mu = np.array(self.icpt[lid], float)
            if mode == 'centroid': mu = np.array([LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_x'], LOCR.loc[lid, 'centroid_y']])
            elif mode == 'icpt': pass
            else:
                B = self.slope[t]
                for k, c in enumerate(cols):
                    if pd.notna(r[c]):
                        mu = mu + (r[c] - self.fm[(t, c)].get(lid, r[c])) * B[k]
            sg = (sx, sy) if mode == 'grid' else (max(sx, 250.0), max(sy, 250.0)) if mode == 'icpt' else (450.0, 450.0)
            out.append((w, mu, np.array(sg)))
        return out

# ---------- landmark factor ----------
POIT = {(t, k): g[['x', 'y']].values for (t, k), g in POI.groupby(['town_id', 'landmark_type'])}
def lm_factor(X, Y, town, ltype, sig, eps):
    P = POIT.get((town, ltype))
    if P is None: return 1.0
    miss = np.ones_like(X)
    for px, py in P:
        miss *= 1 - np.exp(-((X - px) ** 2 + (Y - py) ** 2) / (2 * sig ** 2))
    return eps + (1 - eps) * (1 - miss)

BASE_SIG = {'rooftop': 30.0, 'street': 120.0, 'locality': 500.0, 'pincode': 2000.0}

def posterior(r, prior, vis, cfg, trails=None):
    """vis: DataFrame of this address's visits (already with rho, s). Returns dict with pin, radius, etc. or None."""
    comps = prior.components(r, cfg.get('prior', 'grid')) if cfg.get('prior', 'grid') != 'none' else []
    anchors = [c[1] for c in comps]
    base = None
    if pd.notna(r.geocoder_x) and (cfg.get('use_base', True) or not comps): base = np.array([r.geocoder_x, r.geocoder_y]); anchors.append(base)
    vm = vis[vis.use] if len(vis) else vis
    if len(vm): anchors += [np.array([a, b]) for a, b in zip(vm.ex, vm.ey)]
    if not anchors: return None
    An = np.array(anchors)
    pad = 450.0
    lo, hi = An.min(0) - pad, An.max(0) + pad
    side = max(hi - lo)
    if side > 5200:  # cap: keep window around main modes
        c = np.median(An, 0); lo, hi = c - 2600, c + 2600; side = 5200
    res = max(8.0, side / 330)
    xs = np.arange(lo[0], hi[0], res); ys = np.arange(lo[1], hi[1], res)
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    lp = np.zeros_like(X)
    if comps:
        dens = np.zeros_like(X)
        for w, mu, sg in comps:
            dens += w * np.exp(-0.5 * (((X - mu[0]) / sg[0]) ** 2 + ((Y - mu[1]) / sg[1]) ** 2)) / (2 * np.pi * sg[0] * sg[1])
        if cfg.get('use_poi', True) and r.lm_type and pd.notna(r.lm_type):
            dens = dens * lm_factor(X, Y, r.town_id, r.lm_type, cfg['lm_sig'], cfg['lm_eps'])
        lp += np.log(dens + 1e-14)
    if base is not None and cfg.get('use_base', True):
        sb = BASE_SIG.get(r.precision, 500.0); ob = 0.15
        lp += np.log((1 - ob) * np.exp(-((X - base[0]) ** 2 + (Y - base[1]) ** 2) / (2 * sb ** 2)) / (2 * np.pi * sb ** 2) + ob / AREA)
    vmode = cfg.get('visits', 'robust')

            lp += np.log(1 - cfg['neg_q'] * np.exp(-dmin / (2 * cfg['neg_s'] ** 2)))
    lp -= lp.max(); P = np.exp(lp); P /= P.sum()
    # pin = weighted geometric median over cells holding 99% mass
    flat = np.argsort(P.ravel())[::-1]; cs = np.cumsum(P.ravel()[flat]); keep = flat[:np.searchsorted(cs, 0.99) + 1]
    pts = np.c_[X.ravel()[keep], Y.ravel()[keep]]; w = P.ravel()[keep]
    if cfg.get('pin', 'median') == 'mode': pin = np.array([X.ravel()[flat[0]], Y.ravel()[flat[0]]])
    else: pin = gmedian(pts, w, 25)
    d = np.hypot(pts[:, 0] - pin[0], pts[:, 1] - pin[1]); o = np.argsort(d); cw = np.cumsum(w[o]) / w.sum()
    r50, r90 = d[o][np.searchsorted(cw, 0.5)], d[o][min(np.searchsorted(cw, 0.9), len(o) - 1)]
    return dict(address_id=r.address_id, px=pin[0], py=pin[1], r50=max(r50, res), r90=max(r90, res), res=res, ncomp=len(comps))

def tier(r):
    if pd.isna(r.px): return 'not_geocodable'
    if r.radius_90_m<=75: return 'A_visit_directly'
    if r.radius_90_m<=200: return 'B_visit_with_directions'
    return 'C_verify_first'
P['tier']=P.apply(tier,axis=1)
P['reason']=np.where(P.town_id=='OUT','village/rural address: outside the 3 mapped towns - needs on-ground verification',np.where(P.loc_id.isna()&(P.n_clean==0),'no locality named in text: pincode candidates only',''))

    ang=(np.degrees(np.arctan2(dx,dy))+360)%360; return ['N','NE','E','SE','S','SW','W','NW'][int(((ang+22.5)%360)//45)]

    d=np.hypot(p.x-r.px,p.y-r.py); 
    want=p[p.landmark_type==r.lm_type] if (isinstance(r.lm_type,str)) else p.iloc[0:0]
    if len(want):
        dw=np.hypot(want.x-r.px,want.y-r.py); i=dw.values.argmin()
        if dw.values[i]<=350: parts.append('%s about %d m %s of the pin'%(want.name.values[i],round(dw.values[i],-1),bearing(r.px-want.x.values[i],r.py-want.y.values[i]).replace('N','S') if False else bearing(want.x.values[i]-r.px,want.y.values[i]-r.py)))
    near=p[d<=150].assign(d=d[d<=150]).sort_values('d').head(2)
    for _,q in near.iterrows():
        if not (parts and q['name'] in parts[0]): parts.append('%s %d m %s'%(q['name'],round(q.d,-1),bearing(q.x-r.px,q.y-r.py)))
    loc=LOCR.loc[r.loc_id,'locality_name'] if pd.notna(r.loc_id) else None

    if pd.notna(r.block): grid.append('block %s'%r.block)
    if pd.notna(r.road): grid.append('road %d'%r.road)
    head=(loc or 'locality unconfirmed')+(', '+', '.join(grid) if grid else '')
    return head+'. Landmarks: '+('; '.join(parts) if parts else 'none within 150 m')+'. Pin +/-%d m (90%%).'%round(r.radius_90_m,-1 if r.radius_90_m>=20 else 0)

P[cols].round(1).to_csv(OUT+'/geocoded_addresses.csv',index=False)
print(P.tier.value_counts().to_dict()); print(P.groupby('tier').radius_90_m.median().round(0).to_dict())
print(P[P.tier!='not_geocodable'].groupby('evidence').radius_90_m.describe().round(0))
# integrity tables
vi=V[['visit_id','agent_id','address_id','visit_date','outcome','checkin_x','checkin_y','dwell_s','gps_accuracy_m','photo_hash','f_hotspot','f_dupphoto','f_hard']].copy()
vi['evidence_weight']=np.where(vi.f_hard,0.001,1-vi.agent_id.map(AR).fillna(0)-0.05).round(3); vi.to_csv(OUT+'/visit_integrity.csv',index=False)
ag=V.groupby('agent_id').agg(visits=('visit_id','size'),hotspot_visits=('f_hotspot','sum'),dupphoto_visits=('f_dupphoto','sum'),flagged=('f_hard','sum')).reset_index()
